questions.question: Which of the following are key attributes of Robot Framework's syntax that make it simple and human-readable?

options.text: Space-separated syntax using two or more spaces as separator
Extensive use of special characters for better parsing
options.explanation: Robot Framework reduces the use of special characters to improve readability

options.text: Indentation-based blocks for defining test/keyword bodies
Variables need quotation marks while strings don't
options.explanation: It's the opposite - unquoted strings are considered as strings, while variables need special syntax

options.text: Mostly case-insensitive keyword and variable names

questions.question: What is the difference between User Keywords and Library Keywords in Robot Framework?

options.text: User Keywords are written in Python, Library Keywords in Robot Framework syntax
options.explanation: It's the opposite - User Keywords are written in RF syntax, Library Keywords typically in Python

options.text: User Keywords are written in RF syntax and call other keywords; Library Keywords are typically in Python and interact with the SUT
There is no difference; they are the same thing with different names
options.explanation: They are fundamentally different - User Keywords are high-level, Library Keywords are low-level

options.text: User Keywords can only be used once; Library Keywords can be reused
options.explanation: Both types of keywords are reusable

questions.question: In Robot Framework's file organization, what constitutes a Suite?

options.text: A *.robot file that contains test cases or tasks
Any Python file with keyword implementations
options.explanation: Python files with keywords are libraries, not suites

options.text: A directory containing *.robot suite files
Resource files containing user keywords
options.explanation: Resource files contain keywords but are not suites themselves

options.text: Sub-directories that contain other suites

questions.question: What is the recommended number of spaces to use as a separator in Robot Framework syntax for clarity and readability?

options.text: One space
options.explanation: One space is allowed as a character but not recommended as a separator

options.text: Two spaces
options.explanation: Two spaces work as a separator but four spaces are recommended for better readability

options.text: Four spaces
Tab character
options.explanation: Robot Framework uses space-separated syntax, not tabs

questions.question: What is the difference between Resource Files and Keyword Libraries in Robot Framework?

options.text: Resource Files contain Library Keywords; Libraries contain User Keywords
options.explanation: It's the opposite - Resource Files contain User Keywords; Libraries contain Library Keywords

options.text: Resource Files contain User Keywords and belong to Definition Layer; Libraries contain Library Keywords and belong to Adaptation Layer
Both contain the same type of keywords but in different formats
options.explanation: They contain fundamentally different types of keywords for different purposes

options.text: Resource Files are for RPA; Libraries are for testing
options.explanation: Both can be used for testing and RPA; the difference is in the type of keywords they contain

questions.question:
Consider the following Robot Framework test case:

```robot
*** Test Cases ***
Login Test
    Login User    admin    password123
     Check Dashboard
      Verify User Status
       Logout
```

What is wrong with this test case?

options.text: Nothing is wrong - the test will execute successfully
Keywords should be separated by commas
options.explanation: Robot Framework doesn't use commas to separate keywords

options.text: The indentation must be consistent or the test will fail
options.explanation: While consistent indentation is recommended for readability, Robot Framework will execute this test successfully. Inconsistent indentation is a style issue, not a syntax error

options.text: Test case names cannot contain spaces
options.explanation: Test case names can contain spaces in Robot Framework

questions.question:
Consider the following keyword calls:

```robot
A) Login User    admin    password123
B) Login User admin password123
C) Login User  admin  password123
D) LOGIN USER    admin    password123
E) login user    admin    password123
```

Which of these keyword calls are syntactically correct in Robot Framework? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A) Login User    admin    password123 (4 spaces between elements)
B) Login User admin password123 (1 space between elements)
options.explanation: Single spaces between arguments won't work as separators; need at least two spaces

options.text: C) Login User  admin  password123 (2 spaces between elements)
D) LOGIN USER    admin    password123 (uppercase with 4 spaces)
E) login user    admin    password123 (lowercase with 4 spaces)

questions.question:
Look at this Robot Framework code:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Resource    keywords.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Verify User Creation
    Create New User    John Doe    john@example.com
    ...    role=admin
    ...    department=IT Support
    Verify User Details    john@example.com
```

What does the '...' represent in this code?

options.text: A comment that will be ignored
options.explanation: The '...' is not a comment; it has a specific purpose in RF syntax

options.text: An error in the syntax
options.explanation: This is valid Robot Framework syntax

options.text: Line continuation for the Create New User keyword arguments
A placeholder for missing code
options.explanation: The '...' is the continuation syntax, not a placeholder

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Robot Framework syntax are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Variable names like ${user} and ${USER} refer to the same variable
Keyword names 'Login User' and 'login user' are treated as different keywords
options.explanation: Keyword names are case-insensitive, so these would be the same keyword

options.text: Strings can contain single spaces without quotation marks
Library imports in Settings section are case-sensitive
Test case bodies must be indented relative to the test case name

questions.question:
Consider this Robot Framework code structure:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Documentation    Test suite for user management
Resource    ../resources/common.resource
Library    SeleniumLibrary

*** Variables ***
${URL}    https://example.com
${BROWSER}    chrome

*** Keywords ***
Open Application
    Open Browser    ${URL}    ${BROWSER}
    Maximize Browser Window
```

Which statement about this code is correct?

options.text: This is a test suite file because it contains the Settings section
options.explanation: Without Test Cases or Tasks sections, this would be a resource file, not a suite

options.text: This code represents a resource file structure
The Keywords section can only appear in library files
options.explanation: Keywords section can appear in resource files for user keywords

options.text: Variables must be defined in a separate .py file
options.explanation: Variables can be defined directly in robot files using the Variables section
